description: i014 (SNAPSHOT=s01, branch firmware-table-divisor) complete. One credible finding reported: drivers/gpu/drm/radeon/radeon_atombios.c:3693-3716, radeon_atom_round_to_true_voltage(). Untrusted source: the u16 divisor voltage_step is copied verbatim from the GPU's ATOM BIOS VoltageObjectInfo firmware table by radeon_atom_get_voltage_step() (radeon_atombios.c:3653-3681) from formula->usVoltageStep (optionally (le16_to_cpu(usVoltageStep)+1)/2); the fetch returns success without proving the value nonzero. Violated invariant: the divisor is never validated nonzero at the width where the division executes. Unsafe use: line 3714 `((nominal_voltage - min_voltage) / voltage_step) * voltage_step` divides by the unvalidated firmware value, so a zero/corrupt usVoltageStep yields a kernel divide-by-zero oops. Reachability: sole caller rv6xx_step_sw_voltage() (rv6xx_dpm.c:1272-1290) runs at DPM init from VBIOS-parsed data and additionally would loop forever since voltage_step==0 makes the stepping while-loop non-terminating. Counterevidence checked: the VBIOS interpreter's own divide atom_op_div (atom.c:693-696) guards `if (src != 0)`, proving the convention exists and is absent here; powerplay parsers (ppatomctrl etc.) only divide by sizeof constants; swsmu pptable fields are scaled but never used as divisors. Classified safe: atom.c:694, ppatomctrl.c:107, arcturus_ppt.c:1078. Confidence medium: requires tampered VBIOS with usVoltageStep==0 and a crev-1 voltage object on pre-HD7xxx rv6xx hardware; impact is probe-time DoS (same reliability class as the seed), not memory corruption. Bounded negative evidence: EDID greps found no variable-denominator divisions; of_property_read_* (4516 sites) and acpi_evaluate (632 sites) were only grep-bounded, not line-audited; SMBIOS/EEPROM divisors not separately enumerated.
